149778.overview: A maze shooter created by Clifford Ramshaw & Mark Ramshaw where you shoot the monsters and search for the hidden treasure, shoot them before they kill you.

149779.overview: In this graphic+text adventure game published in Commodore Scene #20, you must find and destroy the evil prince.

149780.overview: The kingdom of Picar is overrun by evil. Only the Sceptre of Lawfulness can save the kingdom. You've to find it in the ancient ruins of the Aranto stronghold.

149781.overview: Evolution is an arcade style action game with six levels where you need to evolve from an amoeba to a human. Each level is a different stage in evolution with it's own unique goals. The first level is the amoeba stage where you need to eat all the DNA on the screen while avoiding the spores, microbes, and antibodies that are trying to stop you. The second level is the tadpole stage. The tadpole needs to eat three flies to move on to the next stage while avoiding the very hungry fish. Next is the rodent stage, where you need to eat five blocks of cheese while avoiding the snakes. In level four you need to guide a beaver across alligator infested waters to retrieve sticks and build a dam. The fifth level is the gorilla stage, where your gorilla has to use coconuts to fight off monkeys that are trying to steel its orange stash. And finally is the human stage, where you have to use a laser gun to fight off mutants that are trying to take over the earth.

149782.overview:
Evolution is a series of six programs which have been divided into three self-contained groups. It represents the evolution of life from the single celled amoeba to modern man, linked by a single theme - survival! Evolution 1 begins with the amoeba stage, in which the player controls the movement of a tiny amoeba which must wander round the screen eating spores whilst avoiding attack from other single celled creatures. In the second program in this suite the player is transformed into a frog which has to dodge from side to side avoiding capture by birds whilst zapping the required number of airborne flies with its tongue. There is no fairy princess as a reward for this one but instant promotion into the form of a beaver in the third program, in which you must swim around and capture ten fish while avoiding contact with a vicious crab. In the next section you control a large gorilla which lumbers round a forest collecting bananas which drop randomly to the ground. The computer controls a small and extremely agile monkey, which makes for tough competition. In the following program you control a caveman who tries to fight off raiders attacking your territory from surrounding caves by firing arrows. Lastly you play as the leader of the global superpower of your choice. you must destroy your enemy's capitals with cruise missiles before you are destroyed by one of their ICBMs. To do this you have a very short time to pre-program the flight of your missile with a series of direction codes as the enemy's missile moves towards your capital. 

From the book "Sixty Programs for the Commodore 64".

149783.overview:
Die Prüfung is a role-playing game in the style of the Bard's Tale series (but with a single character instead of a group). The player takes the role of a magician apprentice who has to roam the overworld in order to solve his final test; split up in five smaller challenges. Of course there are many dungeons to visit and monsters to slain. Combat is turn-based and, when finished successfully, rewards experience points. Those eventually lead to a level-up which improves the statistics (strength, mental, constitution and dexterity) of the player character. As magician, the player also has access to spells which are divided into light, compass, healing, combat and distance. New spells are learned after solving a sub-test.

The interface is split up into four sections: a small windows which shows a picture of the current situation (monsters, world map, conversation partner, 3D dungeon view, etc), a windows with the character's current stats and a list of available orders. Further information, depending on the current playing situation, is available in a big window which takes the whole lower half of the screen, e.g. enemy status, dialogue or automap.

149784.overview: Originally written in Commodore BASIC for the PET this text adventure game has you wield Excalibur and take on the evil that blights the land.

149785.overview: A zero, one or two player board style game created by Ken Smith. This is a section of the 4x4 grid. Is your brain powerful? You will soon find out. Can you Excel? Each move you make adds part of an engine to a square in the 4x4 grid. You score points by getting patterns on the grid. Getting a line of the same part scores 30 points. You add the parts in sequence. Making a complete train backwards or forwards scores 15 points. If you complete a square and both players have parts of the engine you score 30 points. To make a move you enter the grid position. E.G. B2. If you believe you have a point scoring move then press Y to claim.

149786.overview:
The war in the constellation of Vega has finally had catastrophic consequences for the onginarian inhabitants of the walls. Aliens have won and have reduced the entire population to slaves, working in underground mines. Unable to abide this massacre, the Empire has decided to send teams to bring Iberta back to the 7 planets. You are part of one of those groups of rescuers. You will need to do everything possible and use every ounce of power your Exceleron fighter-ship has available to defeat all that will be coming at you. But even if it feels like you are going to die, the trust the Vegans have in you should give you strength to continue. Work to collect the six pieces of shield from around the outside planets which will allow you to then go to the middle planet. If you get past that level then you will be allowed to take on the final confrontation on LEVEL 8.

Published in Commodore User Tape 1988/11 and as Planetoid in Italy in New Special PlayGames n.17 (febbraio 1989).

149787.overview: A game of the "Cassette 50" collection. A game based on the popular TV game countdown. You first may choose the number of letters you wish to play with. Type in the number and hit return. A maximum of 14 letters is recommended, but 8 is the usual number. Then you may choose vowels or consonants one at at time by pressing the V or C key. Then you must make a word from the available letters.

149874.overview: Maneuver Kirby around the level and pick up all the dots without being hit by any of the creatures in this platformer by Mariusz Strawicki and Piotr Strawicki, clear the level and move on to the next fiendish challenge.

149875.overview:
A puzzle\brain game from Norman Anhut (with sound and music by Alexander Herling) where you must push all the colored spheres moved into the X marked spots. But pushing them together or against a wall piece may block your ability to push. Published in 64'er Sonderheft 79, 64'er 1999/04.

The game is pretty much a science-fiction themed Sokoban clone.

149876.overview:
A group of enemy ships randomly make their way across the horizon, and it's up to you to sink as many of them as possible by firing missiles using the space bar. A mobile sight is printed slightly below the line of the horizon. There are three sizes of enemy ships, and the smaller the target the more points you gain. Occasionally the enemy's electronic defense system will succeed in confusing your missile and deflecting it from its course. 
From the book "Sixty Programs for the Commodore 64".

149877.overview: Exodus is a single screen shooter where your task is to stop creatures and objects from escaping 'The Pit', an octagon shape prison where the escapees appear in the middle and attempt to reach the edge. You move your craft around the outside and blast inwards to stop them but you cannot shoot your friend Spud or you lose one of three lives. There is no loss of life for any escapee from escaping unless it is a Llama where you will lose a life if it does reach the edge, and loss of life also occurs if you touch anything on the edge. A timer also counts down, and if it reaches zero then it is game over but you can shoot clocks to increase your time.

149878.overview:
You need to match the two figures on the screen. The red stones transfer to the green no problem. Or is it? "Exor" - an extremely tricky puzzle created by Frederic Thiesse and published in both Happy Computer 1989/04, and in 64'er Sonderheft 54. Puzzle games are as popular as ever. This sharpens your ability to combine and tests your stamina. Brain teasers can also be difficult. »Exor« lets you set the level of difficulty yourself. Everything looks so simple: a seemingly easy task is approached with a shrug. Suddenly it turns out that one had not reckoned with the treachery of the object. The task at »Exor« is also relatively easy. After all, it can't be that difficult to copy a figure from red squares congruently into the adjacent green squares.
Have you ever calculated how many possible variations a matrix of 8 x 8 fields offers?

149879.overview: Side scrolling action game that was released as part of the part of "Fantastic Four 2" game pack compilation.

149880.overview: Expedition Amazon puts you in control of a team of 4 explorers on an expedition to map and study (i.e.: plunder) the ruins of the Incan civilization. Your team consists of a Medic, a Field Assistant, a Radio Operator, and a Guard. After equipping your team with all the necessary supplies (don't forget the mosquito netting!) you travel to your base camp at the edge of the jungle where you will begin your journey. You will quickly meet up with many of the hazards of the jungle as you explore, including hostile natives (hope your Guard is a good shot!), mosquitoes, disease, covered pits, wildlife, and more. Each of your team members has an "EL" rating which indicates how close he is to dying. Death comes quickly for new team members, but as your team gains experience by mapping more and more of the Amazon and Incan ruins, your EL rating goes up and your team members become quite a bit more effective at avoiding hazards. You also get an Efficiency Rating "ER" which is an overall score of your exploration completed and loot collected minus your money spent and the number of team members killed. Once you have mapped a few sectors of jungle you will find some ruins with passages leading underground. Underground is a lot more hazardous than the jungle, as many of the pitfalls you encounter mean instant death if you don't have the proper equipment or your team was not alert. The natives are also a lot more numerous underground as well. But don't worry, you can always replace members of your expedition. Besides, what does it matter if you lost your Field Assistant if the rest of your team is carrying out a bagful of gold and silver?

149881.overview: A Mastermind clone created by Dave Johannsen and published in Loadstar #098. In this game you can imagine that you need to reconstruct a Mastermind game after dropping some pegs off the board. Envision a game of Mastermind where you are ready to put in the final row of pegs that you KNOW are correct, then some pegs are spilled\removed and unable to be retrieved. So you must reconstruct the pieces using logic alone! F1 cycles between background colors. F7 gives you a hint. Q will quit. All puzzles should be solvable only a single way.

149882.overview: A horizontally scrolling shooter created by Afschin Jawari, Amir Jawari and Carl Gustaf Liebe and released in 1992.

149884.overview: Exploding Atoms is an exciting game for two players, which amazes with surprising twists, especially shortly before the end of the game. A screen appears with 6 x 8 fields, occupied by 46 neutral atoms (green) and two player atoms (light blue player 1, dark blue player 2). The players now alternately add an electron to an atom using the joysticks, whereby only neutral atoms and one's own atoms may be supplemented with electrons. If an atom orbits a critical number of electrons! and get another electron!, it explodes and distributes its electrons to the surrounding atoms (which take on the color of the player). Whoever controls all the atoms wins. The more the atoms of the playing field are enriched with electrons, the more surprising turns the game can take. Published in 64'er 1991/10.

149932.overview: Exploding Wall is inspired by the arcade game Arkanoid where you control a bat at the bottom of the screen, bouncing a ball upwards to remove all the bricks on the screen to move to the next level. The difference between this game and the other types off this genre was that it wasn't single screen but allowed you to bounce the ball to the left or right, scrolling the screen when you moved your bat, left or right. Below the playing area is a radar that shows you the position of all the bricks remaining. As you remove the bricks, some will drop a bonus and these include lasers, missiles and slow the ball down. Aliens also move around the screen but you can remove them by hitting them. If you let the ball pass the bat then you lose one of three lives.

149933.overview: After attempting to simulate orienteering with The Forest, Graham Relph takes things a step further by creating a game-world with no fewer than 4 billion locations. These are drawn in considerable detail, and view-able from 2 different modes, as you fly (viewed from above) or walk (viewed panoramic-ally). The task is to locate 9 objects, and you do this by flying close enough to one that a beacon is activated, to which will direct you to it. You must then find a patch of clean land to land on, and then get close by walking to it. Occasionally you will encounter robotic bugs to kill.

149934.overview:
A horizontally scrolling shooter created by Gabriel Winkler and released in Homecomputer 1986/06-07. That was the last radio message from our scout ship SURVIVOR, operating in the galaxy MI3. Apparently the Agamers intend to break the intergalactic truce in order to continue the enslavement of the galaxy. Only TERRA is strong enough to put the mighty enemy in his place, because the allied planets are still too weakened from the last war to be able to do anything against the Agamers. However, we also have our problems, because some of our fleet is still scattered throughout the galaxy and the pitiful remainder is not fully operational either. Therefore we need enough time to mobilize our forces. Time we don't have, for the An-eriil of the Agamer could come at any moment, and we would be left defenseless to face It is therefore your task to launch a surprise attack on the Agamer planet, which should distract them from their plan, until we have assembled enough powerful units.  
 
The aim of this game is to destroy as much as possible with your "heavy cruiser" on the Apamer planet, to confuse the enemy in order to distract him from his actual plan. This is not an easy undertaking, you will certainly soon notice because you will not only be hit by planetary Ädefense forts and heavily fired upon, but pursued by those that wish to destroy you, the entire Agami air force!

149935.overview: COMPUTE!'s Gazette 1993/10, an insert in Compute Magazine. You look around furtively, hoping to see a passage through the tangled mass of rocks and trees. Suddenly you spy an opening in the bushes. You dash through it and pounce on the yellow stone laying on the ground. There! You've finally managed to recover that jewel. Now it's time to explore another maze and find the next jewel.

149937.overview:
A Pong/Arkanoid style game published in 64'er Sonderheft 97 and also in 64'er 1998/06. This game comes with a level editor that can do up to 22 levels. Explosion — blast the energy wall! The deadly barrier Not only on earth, also in the universe living space has become scarce: a wild horde of aliens has chosen our planet to be their new home. A diabolical plan to exterminate humanity... 
 
Highest alert: Forward space watch stations near the asteroid belt report the approach of a colossal armada of space cruisers from the Vega system — apparently Earth is the target. In feverish haste, the World Defense Ministry is mobilizing all available space fleets and interceptors; the nerves of the ground troops are on edge—any second the first deadly laser bomb could hit the surface of the earth! Suddenly the outposts report that the enemy spaceships have stopped immediately after entering the stratosphere, but are in the process of building up a dangerous energy wall in the atmosphere at lightning speed. 
 
at a safe distance, countless space bombs are supposed to wipe out all life on earth. The W.D.O (World Defense Organization) took this emergency into account a long time ago and developed the prototype of an interceptor space cruiser whose energy protection screen is insensitive to all previously known radiation and laser bombs and even throws attacking objects back where they came from!

150000.overview:
Most computer versions of Explosion set out the board for two or more opponents to play on. With this program you are pitted against the computer itself. Are you up to the challenge? Explosion is played on a 3x3 or 4x4 board. 
From the book "Crazy Games for Your Commodore 64".

150001.overview: Of all the mundane tasks which have been turned into action-packed games, bug-repelling must be up there with being a Paper Boy or a Trashman. These aren't average bugs; Chicago is under siege from mutated insects, rats and even toy tanks. You'll have to work through seven houses, each of which has the typical rooms. You control a seemingly-dismembered hand, which must deal with the hordes as they come towards it, into the screen. They can be shot, thumped, or squashed depending on their type. To clear a room you must kill a certain number of creatures in each of the vertically-divided 'lanes' of the room - this causes squares on the ground to change colour.

150002.overview:
The Exterminator is essentially a clone of the arcade game Centipede. A centipede forms from the top of the screen and gradually moves down it, changing direction when striking the many barriers it hits. If it reaches the bottom of the screen, it wins. You control a small droid, which can move up the screen shooting out the centipede, cutting it shorter each time). You can also shoot the barriers, which take multiple hits to remove - the less barriers there are, the longer it will take for the centipede to reach the bottom.

Occasionally a phoenix will appear, either moving horizontally towards the bottom of the screen, or vertically down from the top, to shoot for a points bonus or avoid. You have three lives, but on losing one you gain points for any remaining pieces of centipede. The high score is updated constantly once you pass it, and (unusually for the time) an attract mode demos the game.

150003.overview: Extra-Terrestrial is a single screen side view shooter where it is your mission to destroy an alien invasion that is threatening Earth. You control a missile launcher that starts at the bottom of the screen, which you are able to move around the screen as UFO's appear from above. To fire a missile, you first must load before you can fire by pushing forwards. If you hit an UFO then fallout from the explosion falls to Earth and this must be avoided and if you hit the fallout or a UFO then you lose one of three lives. Before you play, you can select a level (1-3).

150004.overview: Your task in Extreme essentially involves wiping out alien pirates, across 3 distinct sections. This was essentially a spare-time pet project, so you would expect some of the most advanced graphics and special effects you'll ever see. The first level involves flying around in a ship shooting out aliens, with contact depleting your energy (and causing the screen border to flash). The second section involves travelling underwater, running into landmines to set off explosions to kill surrounding enemies. The final part sees you travelling through a building in a huge droid, taking out everything in your path. The game is quite short, and would take around 20 minutes to play through.

150005.overview:
Released as part of the "C64/128 Battle Pack".

The goal of this game is to avoid colliding your spaceship with the planets and meteors as long as you can. You have 10 lives.

150006.overview: Eye is closely based on the board game with the same name. The game is played with two to four players on a board with differently coloured squares. Each player has playing stones of one colour and the goal to get a certain amount of the own stones on the corresponding fields. The spin on this concept is that the board is placed on two rotatable spirals which change the square distribution on the field when used. During each turn, a player has a different amount of moves available (changes depending on the current match situation); each move consisting of moving a square or turning a spiral. This computer version also allows some rule modifications in comparison to the original game and all opponents can be replaced by the AI.

150007.overview: As a mystical shaman, go through a pyramid in ancient Egypt to get the magical eye of horus. In a cool twist, by pressing the up arrow you turn into a birdy and can search through the levels. Just press the down arrow and voila! Human again. Many traps try to trick you.

150010.overview:
You have finally found the long lost Incan Temple here in a jungle clearing.

Now you'll enter in your search for the world's largest diamond, known only in legend as the "Eye of the Inca."

150339.overview: Fantatron\Enemy Soldiers is a game that allows you to display on your screen an epic battle against platoons of enemy soldiers, firing your cannon at them from the lower part of the screen as they attack from above. The fast action can be had with either joystick or keyboard controls. As you progress in the action the soldiers get closer and closer to your ship, hurling more and more bombs at you. Create a passage through by taking down as many of the enemy as possible. If you survive the battle, tougher opponents will follow.

151937.overview: This strategic action puzzle game features original gameplay. You control a spacecraft situated on a globe which you can rotate and move around the screen. You must knock globes into others of the same colour, to rid the screen of all the globes. The screen has no borders, so globes can be pushed off the side of the screen, increasing your tactical range. Knocking globes of different colors into each other produces smaller pods which need to be picked up quickly, giving you energy, or they will turn into globes and you will have to get rid of them too. Many of the globes are linked to other globes (or the ship) via string, and the level layouts include barriers as obstacles (and ricochet points), making the Newtonian physics more complex.

156535.overview:
Fantasy-themed strategic/managerial wargame. The premise is that in a vast continent made up of warring fiefdoms a king arose and unified the whole land. Eventually the once warring barons agreed that they couldn't live peacefully with each other and the king was assassinated while the sole heir was conveniently out fighting in the Crusades. You play one of this barons who must expand his starting territory and conquer the entire kingdom. Gameplay is phase-based and you have to do all sort of things from commanding armies and devicing combat strategies to managing your budding villages and fiefdoms by collecting taxes, recruiting, and balancing your checkbook.

The game includes a series of gameplay options to modify and create your own game modes. You can select the size of the kingdom, the amount of territory to be explored, the chances of random events, and there's even an option that makes the game a race against the clock as you try to get the kingdom before the rightful heir returns. Includes hot-seat multiplayer support for up to 4 players.

159193.overview:
Licensed around former England player Peter Beardsley, this football (soccer) game is viewed side-on. The only playing option is the European Championship tournament of the day, although you can choose the 8 teams from the 26 major European footballing nations of the time (so the USSR, Czechoslovakia and Yugoslavia are all still complete). Two players can compete in these groups, but there's no guarantee of getting straight to a 2-player game, especially as tournaments (and individual matches) can't be quit out of.

The gameplay features variable strength kicks, determined by how long you hold the fire button for. In a break with realistic physics, the ball ricochets back in the direction it came from. Goalkeepers stay on the goal-line rather than using the whole penalty box.

159601.overview:
Olympic Skier is a game where you control a skier over three events, trying to get the biggest score you can before receiving a rating from the computer. The three events are Slalom, Ski-Jump and Downhill and the events don't have to be completed to move to the next one. Slalom is viewed from above at an elevated angle and you ski down the screen which scrolls constantly avoiding obstacles like rocks, logs and trees, while skiing between flags to get to the finish line in the quickest time. You can control your speed, but if you miss three gates or crash, then the event is over.

Ski-Jump is viewed from the side as you move down the ramp while pressing the fire button as fast as you can. When you reach the end, you move to another side view screen, and you try to land safely. You press up for distance, while you press down to land. Downhill is the same as slalom, but you just have to avoid the obstacles and get to the finish in the fastest time again. You are also able to jump, which is needed as obstacles block routes.

159904.overview: Star Trek for Commodore 64 from Interceptor Software. 1983 strategy game that got a rating of 4/5 in Home Computing Weekly magazine. Also released as "Explorer" in Italy.

160617.overview:
There are 50 sub-universes consisting of a central Nucleus surrounded by 32 Orbitals. The sub-universe is called a Aither. The object of the game is to enter the Aither with your ship and destroy enough Orbitals to shut down the Nucleus. Before the Nucleus dies it spits out a Morphi which when destroyed gives you bonus points and money.

Before you deploy your ship from your base you can purchase hulls and weapons. Even sell or scrap the ones that you don't need.

The game is viewed from above your large ship. After deploying from your base you can move about freely in any direction. On the screen you can see your score and a small radar which shows the position of the Orbitals and Nucleus. The further into the game you go and buy more hulls and weapons you will end up with a ship that nearly fills the screen.

160700.overview: A jigsaw puzzle in which you have to re-create a picture of E.T. The Extra-Terrestrial, this is NOT an officially licensed E.T. game. Released as part of "The Big 100" Collection" from Wicked Software.

162083.overview:
In this text adventure, you play the role of Erik the Viking. Upon returning home, you find your farm abandoned; your family has been kidnapped. You gather the things you need for a journey, and go rescue them.

This game combines text adventure with graphics. The graphics illustrate the places you go, and are drawn on the screen as you watch. The display doesn't load a photo. Rather, a pen races around the screen, drawing the pictures in. While the picture is being drawn, the screen flickers.

Although the pictures slow the game down a bit, they are done in a style reminiscent of Viking-age farms. In one scene, you are placed in the center of a longhouse, and they show the depression in the floor, just as can be seen in books.

163891.overview:
Your trusty boat, the Unsinkable 2 enters from the right and drops Dougal in the water. From there you must swim down and collect each of the five encryption keys in turn and take them to the end-portal. Each time a key is used, the display on the portal will show how many more keys are needed. When all keys have been used, the portal will dissolve and Dougal will be able to access the bomb. This must be collected and returned to the boat before the countdown timer elapses. If that happens, it's well and truly game-over... BOOM! 

Successfully returning the bomb to the boat is the goal of each level. Dougal will climb back on board the Unsinkable 2 which will take him off to save the next reef! Any remaining time on the countdown timer will be converted to bonus points before the next level begins. 

On each level there are other collectibles to find. Air cylinders and medipacks replenish air and health respectively. Occasionally the player will come across an alien artifact, no doubt dropped accidentally from a passing flying saucer! Collecting one of these is always a gamble. There are a random mixed bag of about 15 different effects this could have, some good but some bad. 

You must battle your way from reef to increasingly difficult reef until you eventually reach Dr. Drax’s secret dock. That’s your chance to finish him off for good, but be warned- he’s no pushover!

165896.overview: One of the exciting strategy games of power and politics created by Humphrey Walwyn and published in the book, Power Plays on the Commodore 64.

165897.overview:
You are at the edge of Time, closely pursued by a fleet of alien craft who are out to steal your ship’s power. However you have a trick or two up your sleeve. You have the capacity to guard the ends of the time tunnel by setting up energy fields at each of the four open ends of the system. If you attempt to set up a force field anywhere other than at the ends of the time tunnel, the force will feedback and destroy you. Likewise, if you set up a field at the end of an unoccupied tunnel you are finished. Passive cruiser commanders who allow too many aliens through will find their power drained and the game over. 

From the book "Sixty Programs for the Commodore 64" / Your 64 No.02 1984/09.

166249.overview: Adventure Etrusk is a text adventure published in both Personal Software No36 (02/1986) and by Gruppo Editoriale Jackson as part of their Jackson Soft Adventure series, this is a text adventure with some graphics, all text in Italian.

166715.overview:
A French language Lander game coded entirely in BASIC for the C64 by Norbert Bonnefoy . Published by Editions Mondiales S.A. in their French gaming  magazine TILT. TILT No49 Decembre 1987. (program listing starting on page 184).

Controls are keyboard only and use the keys 1 (left), 2 (right), and F7 (thrust).

167237.overview: A collection of educational mini-games for pre-school children, aimed at ages 2½-6 and designed to impart basic skills with letters, numbers and shapes. The exercises include counting, adding and subtracting colored blocks, matching on-screen letters and numbers with the keyboard, memorizing the alphabet, comparing shapes, and practicing basic color drawing. Also published in Stonysoft #0649.

167256.overview: A six-disk, German language only, adventure game with an excellent game font and a really nice challenge. A magician with dangerous magical powers rules over an enchanted valley. Only through clever combinations, questions and actions is it possible to defeat the magician and free the residents. Three double-sided floppy disks with 850 KB adventure and mystery! In more than 150 rooms there are over 70 species on different time planes.

167369.overview: You are on your way to meet your wife and children, traveling by tube from St. Pancreas to Notting Hill, when the train grinds to an abrupt halt in a tunnel. The lights go out and you are in complete darkness. After a few moments the emergency lights come on and after a long 5 minutes with no information the driver announces you must all get of the train. The driver has lost contact with control. Everyone files out through the cab and walks along the track to Russell square. The station is packed with people. Everyone is panicking. Outside there has been a chemical attack! More and more people are pouring into the underground. Can you find your family and escape from London?

168138.overview:
This computer coloring book is another part in the Electric Crayon series and it has 30 pictures of different Zoo inhabitants to color.

Pictures could be colored from a palette of 16 colors. A mix button would "mix" the current color with the 15 other colors and give a total of 256 colors. Choosing a color and clicking in the picture do a color fill in the area clicked. The finished, or in progress, coloring was automatically saved to disk. Player may also remove all colors applied previously to start coloring from the very beginning.

Each picture has an educational description.

Pictures could be printed with, or without, a monthly calendar, description, message, banner, etc.

168214.overview: Krieg um die Krone is the predecessor of Heirs to the Throne a board game comparable with Risk. In a medieval fantasy scenario, which will be automatically created new with every game start, your aiming to eliminate your opponents and conquer the world by placing your armies and attacking neighbor territories. Tactical gameplay is required, because to win the game, you need to conquer those territories filled with treasure chests. In those treasure quests you will find crowns, orbs or scepters. For each of them you receive an title of nobility which improves your ranking and will be rewarded with additional troops. You will win the game if you're able to get all three of them (crown, orb, scepter). Towards most early games of this kind, you don't need an human opponent, you can play as single-player against the AI.

171593.overview:
Imps exist. Just beyond our limited perceptions and in numerous variety. Imps are responsible for your keys going missing or that missing sock from the laundry. Two clans want the imps. The Moebius clan from the 48th plane of existence and the Puckies from the ZX quadrant. Who will be the ultimate victor?

In EFMB: Endless Forms Most Beautiful, you will play as either Moebius or Pucky. To clear a screen, gather all the imps from each level but beware the enemies on some levels. If you move off the screen to the left, you will reappear on the opposite side, one level lower. Moving off the screen to the right is the opposite: you will appear one level higher to the left. Also, there are teleporters on the levels. If you stand on a teleporter and push up or down, you will move up or down one level. Try to clear as many levels as you can.

This is a C64 remake of the 2012 ZX Spectrum game of the same name by Dave Hughes.

171649.overview: Expand vocabulary and word recognition skills. Choose a background and appropriate words to create a picture. Turn the words into images to make interesting scenes and learn new vocabulary. Picture Place! helps children develop reading skills as they play with a word and picture dictionary. Engaging graphics encourage creative play and the recognition of new words.

173082.overview: A vertical scrolling shooter for 1 or 2 (simultaneous) players developed by The Madboars using Chris Yates' Shoot 'Em Up Construction Kit.

176398.overview:
Now available for the C64 - Eye of the Gods.  Take part in a perilous journey through ancient ruins on a quest to find the near-mythical Eye of the Gods, an artifact so powerful it could solve the energy problems of a civilization on the brink of collapse!  Use the special abilities given to you in your morphing power-suit to survive the hazards you encounter on your journey ... The survival of mankind is depending on you!


In the distant future, Mankind has evolved technologically - but this development came at a price:  The resources of the planet were gradually depleted to the point that civilization was left on the brink of collapse.
 
Ancient legends tell that in the origins of civilization, in those times where history is confused with myth, humanity possessed an artifact of great power known as the Eye of the Gods.  Some believe it is a mystical object that connects with other dimensions; others believe it is an inexhaustible source of energy.
 
To calm the voices who plead for the artifact to be recovered, the Army sends one man, you, to infiltrate the ancient ruins of the Cradle of Civilization with one single purpose: Execute a desperate mission to find the Eye of the Gods, and to save humanity from it's own extinction.

Eye of the Gods (C64) 

** EYE OF THE GODS FEATURES ** 

• Huge map to explore!

• Varies enemies to destroy or avoid!

• Morphing power-suit with different powers!

• Retro-style C64 visuals!

176438.overview: Run Like Hell is an Action game, published by Eurosoft, which was released in 1987. Published in Italy as Enchanted Wood in both Logica 2000 n.75 (1988) and in Computing videoteca Nuova serie - Magic Games. To the accompaniment of a particularly good musical background, you will live an exciting adventure inside a splendid and enchanted forest, fascinating for its beauty, but at the same time a den of monstrous and innumerable beasts that infest it. You have a great task in front of you, so you'll need to run like hell!

177441.overview: An early life simulation game from the book "More BASIC Computer Games". Eliza is a program that accepts natural English as input and carries on a somewhat reasonably coherent conversation based on psychoanalytic techniques of Carl Rogers.

177468.overview: A science\educational game that will help you understand the periodic table of elements, published in Loadstar #173. A displayer and tutorial on the most amazing table of all: the Periodic Table of the Elements. The game has a table of 103 of the chemical elements. Each element shown in its order in the periodic chart, and includes its name, atomic symbol, atomic number, atomic weight, discoveries (if any) and date of discovery. After reviewing the info hit F3 to enable the element quiz to test you knowledge.

179418.overview:
Frenzy & Flip Flop (also titled Edufun! Frenzy & Flip Flop) is a release with two educational math games.

In Frenzy, the player must quickly answer 20 subtraction or division questions before a hungry alligator eats 10 fish. If any fish are remaining, the player receives a bonus game where they control a smiling face which tries to capture as many numbers as possible, while avoiding crashing into cherry bombs or mean faces. The smiley face can move in the cardinal directions.

In Flip Flop, the player is shown 10 rounds of 2 figures. The player must decide if the figure on the left can be moved to look exactly like the figure on the right. The player also must state if the objects would match if slid, flipped, or turned. A perfect score receives a special message.

Unlike the Apple II and Atari 8-bit versions, the C64 version was published by Commodore Business Machines themselves.

179702.overview: A stand alone text adventure that builds on the game Hibernated 1, not quite a sequel but the game as seen through the eyes of an unusual and rather unexpected protagonist: Vermin Extermination Unite 4, aka Vlad. Eight Feet Under reveals a previously unknown part of the Hibernated 1 events, so it is essential to complete the main game first. The add-on takes a much less narrative and more puzzle-oriented approach.

180118.overview:
You are the pilot of a ship that must shoot the alien beings that advance from the top of the screen without being hit by their bombs. As the aliens decrease in number they will advance more and more towards your position. You you manage to finish a pattern then you will have to use a lot of quick reflexes avoiding boulders that fall from above. 

Published in Italy under the name E.E.D. in Hit Parade C64 n.28 (Novembre 1988) and in Special Program n.45 (luglio/agosto 1988).

180546.overview: Released at the Commodoremania 2016 Compo and placing sixth in the Mixed Game Competition there. This outstanding set of 5 pinball tables, created with the Pinball Construction Set are somehow crammed into a single disk.

182993.overview: Evil Spiral is a game made by Dan Warren in 2011 using Peter Liepa's Boulder Dash Construction Kit. This version is somewhat unique in that The entire game in in played in a black background, and all the other graphics, including the player sprite is in dark blue.

196386.overview:
Published in the monthly digital magazine Loadstar. ER! is an emergency room simulator/text adventure. You play an intern doctor that is working night shift when patients start rolling in. Nobody to turn to, you have to treat the patients to the best of your abilities.

The game is timed, or how the game puts it, "if you wait too long, unfortunate things might happen to your patients!".
You need to learn your job fast as you need to give far more advanced commands than in most text adventures; for example it might be a good idea to "check patient history" and then "give glucose" to stabilize the patient enough to get her out of the ER.

Published in Loadstar #011.

197369.overview: El Joe is a strange little cross-hair shooter from Italy in which you have to kill people who are riding on what appears to be some kind of bicycles or motor cycles. The goal is to kill as many people as you can before either (a) the time runs out or (b) you run out of ammo.

198628.overview:
Eddy is a simple single-screen platformer with puzzle elements in which you play the titular character of Eddy.

 The goal of the game is to collect all the pots/bags of money before the timer runs out. There are also skulls which you must avoid or jump over. If you hit a skull, then you lose a life.

The game was developed by Joachim Rese and published as a type-in game by Tronic Verlag GmbH in Compute mit 1986/06.

199209.overview: Emix-LX6 is a shoot 'em up that masquerades itself as a racing game. However, despite its looks, it's just a pure vertical scrolling shooter made with SEUCK . It was developed and published by Outlaw-Emix Software in 1991. The game has up to two players playing simultaneous co-op.

202615.overview: By now, it is difficult to believe that you can do almost anything with a computer, but one thing it can't do it romance, but maybe that is wrong. It may not be able to rub your backs or run its fingers through your hair, but this little game might come close. Fun for individual or party play a safe method to have a laugh and let your inhibitions fall aside. Published in Edizione Logica 2000 Supplementi #01 - Logica 2000 N°12 (Dicembre 1985) - Erotic Games.

203590.overview:
Made for the Commodore 64 Crap Game Compo 1999 (C64CGC)

Proceed thru 3 scum-filled levels. The City Streets The Train Yard, where you'll find the President and The Bridge, which is your only means of escape.

At the end of each level you must fight a concentration of enemies, before time runs out. Your success is indicated by the "KILL" meter in the top of the screen.

You begin with 3 lives and you get an extra life at 10000 points intervals.

Story
It's year 1997. You are Snake Plissken, once a warhero, now a criminal. To regain your freedom, you agree to a suicide mission: Rescue the President of United States from the scum-infested ruins of New York.

205189.overview: Somewhere in time and space, you found yourself stuck on the planet Phylom. You have been taken prisoner by the Phyloms - a hostile group of aliens. After managing to escape from your cell, you find you starship and set off to voyage through Phylom and try to escape from the strange planet. Blast your way through every single sector if you can, but the Phyloms are out to stop you from your escapades.

205879.overview: Every Conversation I've Had with Non Gamer Girls at Parties is a brief yet funny text adventure that was developed by Matote using  The Graphic Adventure Creator, and released into the public domain on February 18, 2021.

206719.overview: An educational quiz created in English and Dutch where you learn the Geography of Europe.

207043.overview:
All your favorite Epyx sports games with much faster loading from these titles:
- Summer Games
- Summer Games II 
- Winter Games 
- World Games 
- California Games for Easyflash

207056.overview:
A fast loading compilation that includes:

• Impossible Mission 2 (save game and high scores saved to cart)
• Movie Monster
• Predator USA
• Biggles
• Death Ride

208640.overview: An update to Championship Lode Runner made by 808 and Browny of the The A-Team using the Lode Runner Construction Kit and inspired by the music of the time; New Order, Tears for Fears and Prince.

209009.overview:
In this strategy war game, the goal is to stop the invasion of the extraterrestrial mollusks. The invaders known as the Mollusks reproduce very quickly and do not like water, so there are many ways to stop them. You can dig a hole, which will instantly be filled with water. Laying a mine can blow up four other spaces, filling them with water and if the mollusks move on to these, kaput! You can also spray poison, which will poison the Mollusks reducing their health, but it will also poison the land and lower your score.  
 
To prevent human losses you can evacuate houses using a helicopter. You can also use a rocket to deal instant damage to a certain radius. You will get a new rocket periodically.   
 
The game ends once all Mollusks have been destroyed.

Developed by Dirk Meier and published in Happy Computer 1986/08.

209026.overview:
Help Bramble, Blackberry, and Clover escape to Murky Woods in time to attend that night's music festival.

Originally written as an Adventuron game for browsers, later converted by the author to 8-bit & 16-bit formats using DAAD.

209062.overview:
Ewe Woz 'Ere is our entry into the Reset64 Craptastic Commodore 64 4k Games Competition. This special edition comprises the original game, documentation and a custom loader on a d64 image ready to use in a Commodore 64 emulator or on actual hardware (including original C64, Ultimate 64, C64-mini and more). PAL and NTSC compatible.

Baaary: mutton commando is a cyborg sheep from the future who must preserve the future of mutton-kind by defending the fields from an invasion of meanies.

Armed with a plasma spitter, Baaary is dropped into a field to eliminate all of the meanies. Once all of the meanies in a field are eliminated, Baaary will be collected and moved to the next field that needs clearing.

Some of the later fields may have been affected with stronger or weaker gravity. Be careful not to jump into orbit from fields with weak gravity.

210265.overview:
After quite a few months of work, The Dragon's Castle, the last title of Sputnik World, a game that transports us to a world of medieval fantasy, with heroes, dragons, a couple of dice and all the intention to flood with fun in front of your C64, having a good time and enjoying a new adventure. Open the doors of the castle with the sharp sword and blow the dice, which begins our journey to the treasures that hides our odyssey.  
 
The game is based on the original that Álvaro Ibañez published in Commodore World magazine in February 1987, in his number 34. Its beginning follows the attempt at its preservation that originated in 2013 in a debate at the Commodore forum for its recovery. It has been reworked and rewritten in assembly. Available worldwide in both Spanish and English.

210369.overview: A vertically scrolling homebrew shooter game created with Chris Yates' SEUCK by Kryo and let loose into the world at release party : Breakpoint 2009. In the game you fly into the heavens fighting C64 icons, floppy disks which shoot ones and zeroes at you and other other tech related enemies.

210583.overview: A 3D adventure game created by Richard Bayliss & Joshua Green and published by TND in 2012. It was created with the 3D construction kit. The first ever freescape game from the author, written using the 3D Construction Kit by Incentive/Domark. In this game you are trapped on an alien planet called "Zaphod". You got captured by the aliens and thrown into a prison cell. One of the guards opened the door, but you tricked them. Now it is time to put your escape plan forward. But dare you escape from Zaphod. The music is also written by the creator.

215274.overview: A German language text adventure created by Marcus Ahrens & Holger Schmidt in 1988. Your girlfriend dumped you! Travel around the world to find her and fall in love again.

215275.overview: A Danish text adventure with graphics created by Frans Kappel Øvre and released in 1986. The author translated the game into English but never published it due to low sales of this game. In this text adventure you can carry up to 8 items so make them count. Type bagage to see your inventory. Your goal is to throw the ring of power into the volcano and destroy it and free the world from evil power.

216651.overview:
English Spoken is a French vocabulary program which was aimed to help teach English to French kids and teenagers. 

It was developed by Dominique Lugeol and published as a type-in program in TILT No38 (Janvier 1987).

216760.overview:
That’s a multi-genre, multi-game CRT image for the EasyFlash cartridge.

It’s a Compilation with a lot of games, like:

-    Badlands.
-    Bandits.
-    Boulder Dash.
-    Centipede
-    Frogger.
-    Giana Sisters. ..and so on…
 
This release has many games that use the paddle controls and games utilizing the four-player adapter.

217242.overview:
Eye of the Beholder unofficial version for C64/128. After 16 years, the legendary PC game arrives on the C64 and 128! With Commodore mouse support! This is a full unofficial port of the game Eye of the Beholder, ported from DOS. Consider this as fan art. 
 Features:
-quickstart game with a default party
-flash and disk save option
-open help screen by pressing “H”
-show the map by pressing “M”
-display a bestiary by pressing “B”

218654.overview:
Escalera is a board game from Spain for the Commodore 64 for 1 or 2 players. It was developed and published by Macrisoft in 1986. 

The game is essentially a computerized version of the childhood favorite, Chutes/Snakes and Ladders.

218895.overview: Extend is a Snake variant. The player has to guide a snake through a board. The player must feed the snake with the randomly appearing digits to score points, however feeding the snake makes it grow longer. The higher number, the more points he receives. Number decreasing with time, vanishing after reaching 0.

218915.overview: Eat Yer Pants is an attempt at a "cute 'em up" using the Shoot 'Em, Up Construction Kit. It was developed by Philip and Richard Bayliss and published by Commodore Scene in 2001 as part of their 2001 SEUCK Special.

219216.overview:
A demake of the steam game of the same name. The game was developed by Zoltan Tobler and released into the public domain in 2024.

The C64 version is also known as Elma 64

219663.overview:
EVIL DUNGEON is a BASIC programmed RPG-based Fantasyadventure for the C64.

The story of Alrik, a young adventurer who has to master his first quest. Fight against monsters, search for treasures and plan your next steps to escape the EVIL DUNGEON labyrinth.

219672.overview:
In this deluxe version of the game we follow Baaary: Mutton Commando is a cyborg sheep from the distant future who must preserve the future of mutton-kind by defending the fields from an invasion of Traazkists led by the evil combat lizard, Traazk.

Armed with a basic plasma spitter, Baaary is teleported into the field where he must destroy meanies and collect charges to prime the gateway and clear the level. Shoot the aliens and collect the bonuses which are dropped when they are destroyed in order to progress to the next level!

The goal of each level is to open a gateway by collecting charges which are dropped by the aliens when they are destroyed. When enough charges have been collected, as seen by the charge bar in the status display, it will open somewhere on the level. 

The gateway remains open for a limited amount of time before closing again. Baaary must find it and pass through to destroy all of the aliens and exit the level before the timer expires. The time to find the gateway is short but can be increased by collecting time bonuses. If the gateway closes, it must be re-opened by collecting charges again.

Destroying a meanie might cause it to drop an item or upgrade.

219790.overview: Try to find your Business Partner in a Building with 9 Floors. You can go by Lift by pressing the Number of the Floor. But be careful ... you can also crash & lose your precious life!

219864.overview: Another cool SEUCK game. What's unusual here, like in the prequel, is that you get to play two characters at the same time in the split-screen layout. Be quick or be dead is the thing here.

279607.overview: Elaroo is based around an elephant who bounces around various platforms on a pogo stick, while collecting as many coins as possible.

417523.overview: Evil Wizard II is the sequel to Jesper Lindström's text-based RPG, The Evil Wizard, but re-imagined as a horizontal shoot 'em up. It was developed using Richard Bayliss' and Jonathan Wells' Sideways Shoot 'Em Up Construction Kit mod. The music for the game was made by Anders Carlsson, and the game itself was published by TND in 2012.

417548.overview:
The Evil Wizard is a single-player text based role-playing game (not a text adventure) for the Commodore 64. It was developed by Jesper Lindström and released into the public domain in 2001.

A sequel called Evil Wizard II was released in 2012. However, that was a shoot em up.

Note: The game's text has a lot of typos and grammar errors, probably due to English not being the coder's native language.

418048.overview: Elav is a Commodore 64 game developed by Ice Team in collaboration with Ready64 forum and released in 2006 for the Minigame Competition where it reached the 3° position. This was created to be something of a Rampage clone with only 4KB of space (using music too), so with a space that is less than a 1/10 of normal C64 game. You have 10 levels to clean from the buildings.

421118.overview: Escape Room is an exciting maze-adventure game for Commodore 64.

424179.overview:
Elite: Flicker-Free is a hacked version of the C64 version of David Braben and Ian Bell's classic space trading and space combat simulation of the same name. 

The game itself has not changed, however this is a patched version of Commodore 64 Elite that drastically improves the quality of the graphics. It does this by removing most (but not all) of the flicker from the ship-drawing and planet-drawing routines. 

The hack itself was done by Mark Moxon and released on GitHub in 2023.

A patched version for the Commodore 16/Plus 4 was also released.

425274.overview:
Defend Earth against an attack from space. 
Controls:
A for Left, D for right and S for fire. 
You also have a defense shield that you activate with the space bar.

446846.overview:
Welcome adventurer! «The Elves of Maroland» is the English translation, from the original Spanish, of my first conversational adventure.
Furthermore, this is the port / remake made with DAAD between 2022 and 2024 of the original adventure, made with the legendary PAWS in 1993. An attempt has been made to improve the literature, correct bugs, add new puzzles, etc., but preserving the original story, development and setting.

448167.overview: A zombie horror text adventure game converted by Carmine Migliaccio (TSM) from the original ZX Spectrum game, so you might say it is back from the dead. The game is available in both Italian and English and features slightly animated graphics.

448435.overview: A port of the Atari 2600 game that was in development by Alberto Luviano.  A demo was released on itch.io on May 17, 2024 but was later removed.   The demo consists of a simple but impressive home screen with a quick presentation of changing locations and gameplay similar to the Atari 2600 original.  The demo is in a half-finished state and is missing certain features of the original game, such as the lack of road curves, so for now you can overtake your competitors over a long straight stretch of road.

451557.overview:
This is an effort created in SEUCK, but was one of the very first efforts which had title enhancements. This particular game features a high score, a colourful title screen and other small features. The game itself is a very colourful and well designed effort which makes it one of the better SEUCK efforts seen created with the tool.

It was accepted to be published by Commodore Disk User, originally given to them in 1989 and advertised for release as part of a compilation in late 1990, but the vertically scrolling shooter was never released.

452283.overview: A single screen platformer created by Carl-Henrik Skårstedt of Space Moguls and published as part of a 2024 Reset64 4KB Craptastic Game Competition entry. Game features 13 levels. You've built the most advanced metaverse in the universe, solving the precarious pants problem! But your investors are backing out for blockchain money systems and insane AI bubble projects. You're stuck and need to exit fast while grabbing all the coin you can reach on the way out. You just need to reach the exit. And you are thirteen levels in the hole...

456325.overview: Elevator Eric is a platform game for the Commodore 64. It was developed by Dereks Terrible Software and published by Reset Magazine as part of the 2018 C64 4KB Game Coding Competition.

456359.overview: End of 2023 is a Breakout game where you have to remove all elements of the big 2023 logo. You play with a joystick in port 2 and have to avoid the ball passing your paddle at the bottom of the screen. If that happens, your chance to wipe out 2023 entirely will be over. The game was coded in assember for the One Hour Jame Jam 462 which started on March second of 2024.

456561.overview: EL CARTERO is a platform arcade game in which you play the role of a brave postman traveling around the different corners of the world

456563.overview:
The Second game in Alf Yngve's Cops series.

as with the other games in the series, it was made with the Shoot 'em Up Construction Kit. It was released in 1995.

457453.overview: Eight Links is a Commodore 64 variant of 8 Links by Anton

457537.overview:
The Poison Toad is a simple collect 'em Up for the Commodore 64.

It was developed by Diane Sketchley and published in the UK in Personal Computer News #060 (05.05.1984) and in Spain in Commodore Magazine #05 (07/1984) under the name El Sapo Venenoso.

459220.overview: Inspired by the classics of Infocom, this game invites you on a mysterious journey through time, with a slow-burning narrative that rewards curiosity, observation, and thoughtful reflection. In Echoes of the Future, the text is your map, and language is your tool. Reading carefully and thinking deeply are essential to progress.

459221.overview: Get ready to relive the experience of old-school text adventure games on your favorite retro computer, with all the charm of the ‘80s and ‘90s, as you unravel the secrets hidden on the island of Project Erinia.

459255.overview:
When the big bang is followed by a second earthquake and the sky spews dust and stones - when the flowers lie without life on the hot earth, then the end of the world is near, then it is the twilight of the world.
A game for two players, based on my game "Weltendämmerung" (Twilight of the worlds) from 1993 for Amiga.

460862.overview:
This is a traditional game with a difference. You play it against the computer. The computer knows the rules of the game, but it does not know how to win. At first it makes its moves entirely at random, so you stand a good chance of winning. But, after you have played against it several times, it makes good moves more often and bad moves less often. It learns from its mistakes and takes note of its successes. You may then find it much more difficult to beat it.
This simple game is a fascinating one in its own right. Played against a computer which is capable of learning to improve its play is a somewhat unusual experience. 

Published in the book "The Commodore 64 Games Book - 21 Sensational Games".

461345.overview:
Epyx Epics is a 1988 European exclusive compilation pack for the Commodore 64, and published by U.S. Gold.

The compilation pack includes the four following previously released games:

- Breakdance
- Impossible Mission
- Pit Stop II
- Summer Games

Breakdance, Impossible Mission, and Pit Stop II all came on the same cassette, whereas Summer Games came on a cassette all by itself, due to the game taking up two sides.

462064.overview: Enjoy the new, remastered version with new SID music by NORDISCHSOUND, a new interface, save option

462908.overview: In this delirious platformer, you control The Chef, a friendly cook with a big mustache and a fiery temper. Your mission: collect all the bags of flour and magic eggs before you burn the cake!

463266.overview:
Elicoph is a simple 1-player only duel shooter for the Commodore 64.

You play a helicopter as you battle against a computer controlled U.F.O.

The game was developed and released by Ice Team on July 28, 2002 as an entry into Minigame Competition 2002.

464771.overview: A single-player SEUCK game developed by Igor Ertazikin (with music by Richard Batliss) and was part of the Sideways SEUCK Game Creation Compo 2015.

466124.overview: You are the last surviving crew member aboard Spaceship Seven, which has been boarded by aliens. You must find a way to escape the spaceship.

466568.overview: Peg Solitaire is a single-player puzzle game played on a board with holes and pegs. The goal is to remove pegs by jumping one peg over another into an empty hole, similar to checkers. The jumped peg is removed from the board. Moves are allowed only horizontally or vertically, not diagonally. You continue making jumps until no more moves are possible. The challenge is to finish the game with as few pegs left as possible—ideally just one.

471451.overview:
A first-person shooter for the Commodore 64 inspired by Wolfenstein 3D.

The game also includes a built-in level editor.

471856.overview: Evil Spirit is an adventure game in which the protagonist is stranded in a dark place and must fight for survival. The game world is explored from a first-person perspective and contains various puzzles as well as a number of hostile creatures.

472379.overview:
Elektrosmog is a small maze game for the C64. It was created as a study project in 2008/2009 while attending a University of Applied Sciences.

The game itself is quite simple and nothing special really, but it was my first C64 machine language project, and the download also includes the full source code and a PDF with the project's documentation (in German language).

So, if you are interested to learn a little bit about C64 machine language / assembly language coding, this package might be of interest for you. Note that this is not a full tutorial, though, so you might need some more material. But it serves as a nice first read, I guess. Also, the source code is of course not perfect, but it's well-commented and structured, so you should also be able to get something out of it.

The game was created using the ACME assembler.

474594.overview: Steers a snake around a walled play-field. Eat tacos (food) to grow and score

479016.overview: Within each room, the player controls Eyedball, moving him left or right and guiding him down from one platform to another. The character must avoid various obstacles and spooky foes in order to recover his comrades transformed into hearts. Our hero has no defenses against enemies, but he possesses an extraordinary magical power: the ability to rotate his surroundings, allowing him to reach parts of the room that would otherwise be inaccessible.

480494.overview: This game was originally a C128 type-in program from the October 1987 issue of Ahoy magazine. It has now been converted to the 64 and slightly enhanced with new font and music plus a special winning screen. The option to select how much money that you begin with has been added as well. Choose from the default $500 all the way up to $10,000.

480741.overview: A creepy little adventure with multiple endings. Enjoy!

480746.overview: Everybody name-drops ELIZA when they talk about AI

481022.overview: E.T.: The Extra-Terrestrial is a side-scrolling platform game, in which E.T. has to grab sweets, avoid shots coming from the left and jump over spikes.

481675.overview: A virtual pet in your pocket… well, on your Commodore 64.

481991.overview: For the first AI game competition at Lemon64.

482131.overview: Ecos is a wave shooter for the Commodore 64 and PC with a twist: you don't have lives, you have three time jumps. Every time you are hit, the wave starts over and your recorded attempt comes back as a ghost ship, an echo, repeating every move and every shot. Up to three echoes fly with you at once. Fall wisely, and your past selves become your squadron.

482209.overview: No pitch, no players to steer – just pure league excitement! 40 fictional top clubs from 11 European countries battle it out in two divisions of 20 clubs.

482827.overview: ECOS - BATTLE TANKS  is a top-down tank duel for the Commodore 64. Two tanks hunt each other through single-screen mazes, grab weapons and medkits, dodge mines, and can unleash their Echo: a ghost tank that joins the battle on its own.
